title: KRG President Nechirvan Barzani in Baghdad for Government Formation Talks with PM-Designate Zaidi
detail: Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani arrived in Baghdad on May 4, 2026 for two days of government formation talks with PM-designate Ali al-Zaidi and Coordination Framework leaders. Core Kurdish demands centered on: public-sector salary arrears owed by Baghdad to Kurdistan government employees (unpaid for months due to the oil revenue crisis), Peshmerga budget transfers under the 2005 constitutional framework, implementation of Article 140 (Kirkuk and disputed territories status), and equitable oil revenue sharing. Al-Zaidi pledged to address the salary issue as a priority in his first 100 days. The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) sought guarantees before committing its parliamentary bloc to the confidence vote. The talks reflected the enduring challenge of Kurdish integration into Iraq's federal system.

media.caption: KRG President Nechirvan Barzani meets PM-designate Zaidi in Baghdad — Kurdish demands include salary arrears, Peshmerga budget, and Article 140 implementation

title: ISIS Claims First Publicly Attributed Attack on Iraqi Army in 2026
detail: The Islamic State's Iraq Province issued a claim of responsibility for an attack against Iraqi Army forces on May 4, 2026, marking the group's first publicly claimed operation in Iraq for 2026 according to MEMRI's Jihad and Terrorism Threat Monitor. The attack came as ISIS continued its shift toward lower-profile insurgency activity in the wake of the broader regional war, which had diverted security resources and attention from counterterrorism operations. ISIS's post-2017 insurgency in Iraq — sustained primarily in Anbar, Diyala, Kirkuk, and Salah al-Din provinces — has averaged approximately 500 incidents per year since the territorial defeat, though publicly claimed attacks declined significantly in the 2024–2025 period as operational security was tightened.

title: PM-Designate Zaidi Submits 14-Pillar Governance Program to Parliament; Confidence Vote Scheduled
detail: Prime Minister-designate Ali al-Zaidi submitted a detailed 2026–2029 ministerial program to the Iraqi Council of Representatives on May 4–5, 2026, spanning 14 policy pillars including security sector reform, oil revenue diversification, anti-corruption measures, infrastructure investment, and KRG-Baghdad relations. Parliament scheduled a special plenary session for the confidence vote by the end of the following week (approximately May 8–9). The program signaled Zaidi's intent to present himself as a technocratic reformer rather than a sectarian political figure, consistent with his non-political background as a businessman. Political analysts noted the program's substance would be tested against the entrenched muhasasa patronage system and PMF power centers.

media.caption: PM-designate Zaidi presents 14-pillar governance program for 2026-2029; parliamentary confidence vote expected by end of week
